findings.comment: The nozzles on the soda machines were observed with an accumulation of soil. The PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training for the third party food worker. The employee said that they had the certification however was unable to pull up the certification. Education was carried out. The facility will contact the third party company responsible for food prep to ensure that the employees coming to the facility for food prep have the relevant paperwork. Inspector will return on 10/8/2026 to follow up on the food handler training. Ensure that all food employees are trained in food safety and food handler are available for verification at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present during today’s inspection. At the end of the inspection, the manager with a CFPM arrived. PIC was made aware that there needs to be at least one certified food protection manager present during the facility’s operational hours at all times. PIC ensured inspector that come next inspection, there will be a certified food protection manager present.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of mold in the ice dispenser of the polar pop soda machine. PIC was made aware of the mold build up and the ice dispenser was cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to avoid food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed visible light from the back exit door. Discussed with pic and pic said that they are currently working on getting the gap seal by management. Ensure the necessary repairs are done to seal the gaps to avoid the entry of rodents and other pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(E) Outer Openings, Protected. (E) Paragraph (D) of this section does not apply if flying insects and other pests are absent due to the location of the establishment, the weather, or other limiting condition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty water being stored in mop bucket with the mop head stored in it. PIC was made aware of the appropriate procedure for storing mop heads and the mop wastewater disposal. Ensure that wastewater after mopping are disposed properly and mop heads are stored appropriately to discourage pathogen distribution and growth.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of dust/food debris:
-The pipes under the walk-in cooler units need to be cleaned as they have dust accumulation.
-The floor under the soda syrup racks has an accumulation of soda syrup and will need to be cleaned. 
Ensure these areas are cleaned to remove their current accumulation of soils and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
